title: Undo of a sent reminder's draft says it undid it; the letter stays sent
body:
## Summary
`draft_reminder` is declared reversible, and its undo deletes the draft only `AND sent_at IS NULL`; once the draft has been sent, undo deletes nothing, yet `undoActivity` marks the row undone and logs 'Undid #N: Drafted a ... Not sent.' (examples/ledgerbox/app/actions.ts:511-512).

## Description
`applyUndo`'s `reminder` case (examples/ledgerbox/app/actions.ts:511) runs `DELETE FROM reminders WHERE id = ? AND sent_at IS NULL`. `undoActivity` (examples/demo-kit/src/activity/index.ts:114-135) does not look at what the case changed: it sets `undone = 1` and appends an 'Undid #N' row whatever happened. So the Trail and `undoAction`'s answer both say a reminder was taken back that had already reached a person - the act most needing evidence is the one whose record is now false. This is the observability failure the lens names: a privileged outcome (a sent letter) whose audit row is contradicted by the undo row after it. Fixed looks like: the `reminder` case throws (or returns a refusal) when the row is already sent, so the transaction rolls back and `undoAction` answers ok:false with 'already sent - a sent reminder cannot be taken back'. Technique: mcp-tools/tool-schema-design, 'publish them honestly is a test' - the act's reversibility is conditional and the undo must say so. The new class-parity test in test/ledgerbox-domain-lib.test.ts drives each act's undo immediately and cannot see this order.

## Flow
- agent drafts a reminder (AUTO), then sends it (GATED, approved)
- someone presses Undo on the earlier draft row in the Trail -> undoAction(draft id)
- applyUndo deletes 0 rows; undoActivity marks the draft row undone and logs 'Undid #N: Drafted ... Not sent.'
- observed: undo ok:true, the reminder's sent_at unchanged
- fix: the reminder case refuses a sent row, in examples/ledgerbox/app/actions.ts (app-shell's file), with the test above

## Expected impact
Whoever reads the Trail (a person, or Athena recalling it) sees the letter as taken back when it went out; measured as undo answers for a sent draft (1 of 1 says ok today). Could break: an undo flow that relies on undo always succeeding for drafts.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - an undo that reversed nothing never reports that it did
Before: probe on the seeded books (2026-10-16): draft LB-2026-0029, send, undo the draft row -> ok:true, reminder sent_at still set, newest activity 'Undid #2: Drafted a gentle reminder for LB-2026-0029 ...'
After: predicted ok:false with a reason, no undo row, sent_at unchanged
Method: simulation - the Before is a probe, but the fix lives in app/actions.ts, outside this round's write set, so the After could not be taken
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: a test in examples/ledgerbox/test/: draftReminderAction, sendReminderAction, then undoAction on the draft's activity row; expect ok:false with a reason, no 'Undid' row, `undone` still 0 - seeded red on today's applyUndo

title: mark_paid and match_bank_line apply money to a draft nobody owes
body:
## Summary
`markPaidAction` refuses only a void invoice and `matchAction` refuses neither void nor draft (examples/ledgerbox/app/actions.ts:162, :280), so money can be recorded against a draft that `COUNTED_OUT` says is billed to nobody.

## Description
lib/db.ts `COUNTED_OUT` (void, draft) is the books' statement that a draft is not a debt: `summarize`, the lanes (6e5479b) and the credit offer (`takesCredit`, 4bcdc24) all leave it out. The two acts that apply money do not: `markPaidAction` (app/actions.ts:280-289) checks `state === 'void'` only, and `matchAction` (:162-178) checks only that the line is unapplied and not larger than the balance. A probe recorded $10.00 against the seed's draft LB-2026-0055 with ok:true; that payment then counts nowhere (the invoice is out of every total) while the money is applied. mark_paid is PERMANENT, so the payment cannot be taken back by Undo either. Fixed looks like: both acts refuse `COUNTED_OUT` states with 'LB-2026-0055 is a draft - send it before recording money against it.', from the same list.

## Flow
- agent or person calls mark_paid(LB-2026-0055, 10) or match_bank_line(LB-2026-0055, <credit>)
- markPaidAction: not void -> INSERT payments; ok:true
- the draft still reads `draft`, out of every total, with a payment under it that nothing shows
- fix: refuse COUNTED_OUT in both acts (app/actions.ts, app-shell's file) with the test above

## Expected impact
Nobody can record money against an invoice the client was never sent; measured as payments accepted on a draft (2 of 2 acts accept today). Could break: a demo beat that pays a draft on purpose (none found).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no act applies money to an invoice the books count as owed by nobody
Before: probe 2026-10-16: markPaidAction('inv_0055', 1000) -> ok:true 'Recorded $10.00 against LB-2026-0055.'
After: predicted ok:false from both acts, payments unchanged
Method: simulation - Before is a probe; the fix is in app/actions.ts, outside this round's write set
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: a test in examples/ledgerbox/test/: markPaidAction and matchAction against the seed's draft (LB-2026-0055) expect ok:false and no payments row - seeded red today

title: buildSheet re-reads and re-scores every actionable invoice per render
body:
## Summary
`buildSheet` (examples/ledgerbox/lib/lanes/index.ts:127-165) calls `getInvoiceDetail` for each of ~70 actionable rows; each call re-runs ROW_SQL's five correlated subqueries for a row `listInvoices` already holds, re-scores candidates against the whole pool, and runs five more queries.

## Description
`getInvoiceDetail` (lib/db.ts) starts with `getInvoice(id)` - the same ROW_SQL row `listInvoices()` returned moments earlier - then `candidatesFor` over `unappliedLines()` (the scoring `toRow` already did), then clients, invoice_lines, payments, matches and reminders, one query each. Under `node --test`, where `cache()` does not memoise, one buildSheet+buildBooks made 599 database calls and took a median 102 ms (n=10, 2026-10-16, seeded books). Under Next the memoised readers drop out, but the per-row detail does not: about six queries and one full candidate scoring per actionable invoice on every page render. Fixed looks like: build the detail from the row `listInvoices` already scored (its candidates kept rather than counted), and read lines, payments, matches and reminders in one query each for all actionable ids.

## Flow
- the page renders -> buildSheet -> for each actionable row getInvoiceDetail(id)
- getInvoice re-runs ROW_SQL for that row and re-scores its candidates; five further queries follow
- fix: keep the scored candidates on the row, batch the four child reads by invoice id

## Expected impact
Faster first render of the one shipped page and less SQLite contention for the server actions; measured as db calls and ms per render on both arms. Could break: the card's candidate slice (DETAIL_CANDIDATES) and order, which must stay identical.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one page render reads each invoice once
Before: 599 db calls, 102 ms median per buildSheet+buildBooks with cache() inert (node --test probe, n=10)
After: predicted ~ (fixed reads + 4 batched) per render; not measured under a request-scoped cache
Method: simulation - the Before is a probe without React's request memo; the honest figure needs the emulated request, which the round did not build
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a probe that counts db.all/db.get calls and times buildSheet()+buildBooks() over one emulated request (react cache() honoured), on both arms

title: Manifest restates the kit's zoom-verb parameters by hand, untested
body:
## Summary
examples/ledgerbox/lib/manifest.ts:77-92 types out `open_group(id)`, `open_item(id, group?)` and their descriptions, while `useZoomTools` (examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/zoomTools.ts:121-165) registers the real ones; nothing checks the copy.

## Description
The manifest is 'what the surface prints and what the test counts' (lib/manifest.ts header), and tools.test.ts checks it against TOOL_CLASSES - but the four zoom verbs' parameters are registered by the kit, not by `registration()`, so a change to the kit's parameters (a rename, a new required one) leaves the printed register and the tests describing tools the page no longer offers. Technique mcp-tools/tool-schema-design: 'the published schema and the enforced schema must be the same artifact'. The kit's `open_item` also takes only an exact id (zoomTools.ts:165) while every other invoice-taking tool takes an id or a number (lib/invoice-ref.ts), which the copy hides.

## Flow
- the kit renames open_item's `group` parameter
- lib/manifest.ts still prints `group`; tools.test.ts and journey.test.ts stay green
- fix: the kit exports the four specs' parameters; the manifest imports them; a test pins equality

## Expected impact
The register an agent and a person read stays the one the page registers; measured as differing parameter names between the two (0 today, unguarded). Could break: nothing at runtime.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one statement of the zoom verbs' parameters
Before: 2 hand-kept lists, 0 tests tying them (grep: no test imports zoomTools' parameters)
After: 1 list, 1 test
Method: simulation - the source of truth is in examples/demo-kit, another context's files
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/ledgerbox/lib/manifest.ts:77-92  { name: "open_group", parameters: [{ name: "id", ... }] }, { name: "open_item", parameters: [id, group] }
examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/zoomTools.ts:121-165  useWebMCPTool({ name: "open_group", parameters: [...] }) ... useWebMCPTool({ name: "open_item", parameters: [...] })
instrument: the kit exports its zoom verbs' parameter arrays (a pure spec beside useZoomTools); a test in examples/ledgerbox/test/ compares VIEW_CAPABILITIES' read_view/open_group/open_item/zoom_out parameters to them

title: The close counts interest, savings and a VAT refund as unapplied lines
body:
## Summary
`summarize`'s `unmatched_lines` / `unmatched_cents` (examples/ledgerbox/lib/db.ts) and the mast's `unmatchedCount` count every unapplied incoming line, so 4 of the quarter's 19 - $3,410.62 that no invoice will ever match - sit in the close's 'Bank lines unapplied' figure.

## Description
The seed's OTHER_CREDITS (examples/ledgerbox/lib/seed-fixtures.ts:81-86: interest $4.12, a $2,500 transfer from savings, an $843 VAT refund, a $63.50 rail refund) are incoming lines with no invoice behind them. `summarize` filters unapplied lines by direction and period only, so the export reads 'Bank lines unapplied 19 worth ...' and a reader takes it as client money waiting to be reconciled. Nothing on `bank_lines` says what kind of credit a line is, so leaving them out needs a decision: a `kind` column the import sets, a rule (no plausible invoice and not from a client), or a separate 'other credits' line in the close. That is a product call about what the close reports, not a defect fix.

## Flow
- export_summary('quarter') -> 'Bank lines unapplied 19 worth $X'
- 4 of those lines are not customer payments; no match will ever clear them
- options: classify at import and report them apart; or keep and rename the line

## Expected impact
The close's unapplied figure stops overstating unreconciled client money by $3,410.62 (quarter). Could break: the mast's unmatched count and any beat that counts 19.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the close's unapplied credits are client money only
Before: 19 unapplied incoming lines in the quarter, 4 of them non-customer ($3,410.62)
After: 15 customer credits reported, the 4 named apart (if the classification is chosen)
Method: probe - counted on the seeded books; the After depends on the chosen rule
Result: better
Gate: direction
